events.title: Smoke Gets in Your Eyes
events.text: Congress has done it. From today, cigarettes can no longer be advertised on television or radio. The tobacco men are furious, and their budgets are looking for a new home.

options.label: Move them to billboards and magazines
options.result: Our tobacco clients appreciate the hustle. Print and outdoor it is.

options.label: Drop tobacco and keep our hands clean
options.result: We'll never work for a cigarette company again. The banks noticed.

events.title: The Hilltop Jingle
events.text: A rival agency just put two hundred kids on a hilltop, singing about a soft drink. The whole country is humming it. Every client on Madison Avenue wants a song now.

options.label: Ride the trend
options.result: Jingles will land harder for the next year.

options.label: Zig when they zag
options.result: The team studies what everyone else is missing.

events.title: Pong!
events.text: A little company in California called Atarii has put a game in a bar. Two paddles, one dot, and a line of people waiting to play it. Strange times.

options.label: Ping pong on a TV? Huh.
options.result: Atarii is now out there, looking for an agency.

events.title: The Oil Shock
events.text: The oil embargo has hit. Gas stations are running dry and the big car makers, airlines and oil companies are cutting their ad budgets. The small-car people are suddenly very popular.

options.label: Sell thrift: pitch the economy cars
options.result: An automaker opens a pitch for a fuel-saving campaign.

options.label: Stand by Big Oil
options.result: The oil men won't forget it. The carmakers might not either.

events.title: Belt Tightening
events.text: The economy is in a slump. Every client is trimming its ad budget by ten percent for the year. The bank manager is suddenly very interested in our books.

options.label: Cut salaries by ten percent
options.result: Payroll is lighter. So is the mood in the office.

options.label: Take a bank loan
options.result: The loan is in the account. Monthly repayments start next month.

options.label: Ride it out
options.result: We keep calm and carry on.

events.title: Spirit of '76
events.text: America turns two hundred this year. Every client wants red, white and blue on everything. You can hardly see the product for the flags.

options.label: Wave the flag
options.result: Emotional campaigns will land harder this year.

options.label: Be the joke in a room full of flags
options.result: Humor will stand out this year.

events.title: Two Guys in a Garage
events.text: Two long-haired kids from Apricot Computer want a campaign for their home computer. They can't pay much, but they're offering a slice of the company instead.

options.label: Take the shares
options.result: We now own a little piece of a computer company. Probably worthless.

options.label: Cash only, boys
options.result: They scraped the money together. Nice kids.

options.label: Show them the door
options.result: Computers in the home? Never going to happen.

events.title: A Galaxy Far Away
events.text: A space movie has taken the country by storm and every kid wants the toys. The toy makers are doubling their budgets and looking for agencies that can keep up.

options.label: May the sales be with us
options.result: Toy budgets are up for the next two years.

events.title: Deregulation Takes Off
events.text: Washington has deregulated the airlines. New routes, new fares, new upstarts. Every airline is suddenly fighting for its life and shopping for a new agency.

options.label: Buckle up
options.result: Expect more airline pitches, and less airline loyalty.

events.title: Gas Lines Again
events.text: A second oil crisis. The lines at the pumps are back, odd and even days and all. Car, airline and oil budgets shrink again.

options.label: Sell thrift again
options.result: An automaker opens a pitch.

options.label: Stand by Big Oil
options.result: The oil men appreciate a friend.

events.title: Apricot Goes Public
events.text: Remember those two kids from the garage? Apricot Computer just went public, and our little slice of the company is worth a fortune.

options.label: Sell the shares
options.result: The champagne is on the agency tonight.

options.label: Hold. They'll be worth more one day.
options.result: The trade press calls us visionaries.

events.title: Video Killed the Radio Star
events.text: A new cable channel plays nothing but music videos, all day long. The kids can't look away. The eighties are here.

options.label: Turn it up
options.result: The team is already sketching ideas for the new decade.

events.title: Dinner at the Oak Room
events.text: The chairman of {client} invites you to dinner at the Oak Room. Dark wood, white tablecloths, and a man who has never once smiled in a meeting.

options.label: Order the steak and a martini

effects.winText: He orders the same. By dessert you're old friends.
effects.loseText: He drinks club soda. The evening never recovers.

options.label: Walk him through the campaign plan

effects.winText: He loves the numbers. He asks for a copy.
effects.loseText: He checks his watch twice. Shop talk at dinner was a mistake.

options.label: Let him do the talking
options.result: Three hours on golf and the gold standard. He calls it a wonderful evening.

events.title: Three-Martini Lunch
events.text: The marketing chief of {client} likes his lunches long and his martinis dry. It's one o'clock and he's ordering the second round.

options.label: Keep up with him
options.result: He calls you a real ad man. You don't remember the afternoon.

options.label: Switch to coffee
options.result: He raises an eyebrow, but signs the check.

events.title: A Night at Studio 55
events.text: {client} is throwing a party at the hottest club in town, and you're on the list. Velvet ropes, mirror balls, and a doorman who decides your fate.

options.label: Put on your dancing shoes
options.result: You dance until four. The client is thrilled.

options.label: Politely decline
options.result: Someone from another agency took your spot on the list.

events.title: The Nephew
events.text: The president of {client} has a favor to ask. His nephew just graduated and needs a job. "He's a creative type," he says. "Mostly."

options.label: Find the boy a desk
options.result: The nephew starts Monday.

options.label: We're not hiring right now
options.result: The president takes it well. Mostly.

events.title: An Invitation to Pitch
events.text: A letter on heavy cream stock: {client} is reviewing its advertising and would like {agency} to pitch for the account.

events.title: Word Gets Around
events.text: {client} heard at the club that we're pitching for one of their rivals. Their marketing director called to say it's over.

events.title: A Regional Shop
events.text: The trade press has started calling {agency} "one to watch". Medium-sized clients are taking our calls now.

events.title: Madison Avenue
events.text: {agency} made the Ad Age list of agencies that matter. The biggest names in the country will now invite us to pitch.

events.title: Account Under Review
events.text: {client} isn't happy with how this year went. Their lawyers are reading the contract, and other agencies are already calling them.

effects.winText: Over brandy, they agree to give us one more year.
effects.loseText: Dinner was lovely. They're leaving anyway.

options.label: Offer a free extra campaign
options.result: They'll stay, and they expect one more campaign this year at our expense.

options.label: Let them go
options.result: We part ways, politely.

events.title: Poached
events.text: Sterling Crane has offered {staff} a corner office and a bigger salary. They want to know if we'll match it.

options.label: Match the offer
options.result: {staff} stays, at a price.

options.label: Wish them luck
options.result: {staff} packs up their desk.

events.title: Creative Block
events.text: The team is stuck. Nobody has had a good idea in weeks, and the wastebasket is full of crumpled paper.

options.label: Everybody to the bar, on the agency
options.result: Somebody had a great idea on a napkin around midnight.

options.label: Push through it
options.result: The team grinds on, a little slower.

events.title: The Leaked Deck
events.text: A courier has delivered the wrong envelope. Inside is the full pitch a rival agency is preparing for {client}.

effects.winText: Nobody will ever know. Our pitch just got sharper.
effects.loseText: The courier talked. The trade press is calling us cheats.

options.label: Send it back unopened
options.result: The rival agency sends a thank-you note. Word gets around.

events.title: The Clio Call
events.text: Our work for {client} could be nominated for advertising's biggest award. The entry fee isn't cheap, and there's no guarantee.

effects.winText: We won! The statue goes on the reception desk.
effects.loseText: We lost to a soap commercial. Next year.

options.label: Save the money
options.result: Awards are for agencies with time to spare.
